name: Holy Roman Empire
alt: Holy Roman Empire of the Middle Ages

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Germany
predecessors.text: the whole realm of Otto I, the German kingdom and, from late 961, Italy

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Italy
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Italy shape of 962-969, 623 of whose 657 cells lie inside this dossier's 962 shape

successors.name: Holy Roman Empire (1260-1806)
successors.text: the Empire's directly held lands from 1260, Cliopatria's second row for the same empire

capitals.name: Itinerant court (Frankfurt and Aachen named for elections and coronations)

ledger.x: 962: Otto I is crowned emperor in Rome and the Empire begins.
970: Cliopatria hands the March of Spoleto and Camerino lands to the Duchy of Benevento.
970: Cliopatria's shape adds Corsica to the Empire; the Otto I page has 'Corsica or Sardinia: not on page'.
983: the Obotrites join the revolt and the Billung March goes.
983: the Slav revolt takes the Elbe-Oder marches.
985: 'From 985, several princes of the Empire carried out annual campaigns' to win back the lands east of the Elbe; the Elbe line holds and the Slav lands stay in dispute until the alliance of 1003.
990: Cliopatria returns the central Italian cells (Spoleto, Camerino, Marche, Abruzzo) from the Duchy of Benevento's shape to the Empire.
1002: Bolesław I of Poland takes Meissen and Lusatia.
1002: Arduin of Ivrea 'proclaimed himself King of Italy at Pavia soon after the Emperor's death', setting up a rival kingdom in Lombardy against the German king.
1003: Cliopatria's 1003 shape also drops 36 cells in Lower and Upper Austria (and 6 in Bavaria) to its Kingdom of Poland shape.
1003: the Empire changes course in the east: 'In 1003 King Henry II of Germany tried a different approach: he allied himself with the Lutici and waged war against Bolesław.'
1004: Henry II opens his war with Poland.
1004: Henry II is crowned King of Italy at Pavia on 14 May 1004.
1010: Cliopatria's shape takes back Bohemia, Meissen and Lusatia from its Poland shape.
1010: the Republic of Pisa begins in Cliopatria and takes 12 cells of the Empire's Tuscan coast.
1010: the Republic of Genoa begins in Cliopatria and takes the Empire's Ligurian coast.
1018: Lusatia and Meissen stay with Poland as a nominal fief: 'Poland kept Lusatia and Meissen, which Bolesław held on purely nominal terms of vassalage.'
1018: the war with Poland ends.
1024: the Salian dynasty succeeds the Ottonians.
1028: war with Poland resumes: Mieszko II 'took the initiative and invaded Lusatia'.
1029: Moravia returns from Poland to Bohemia, then an Imperial duchy.
1031: Mieszko II surrenders: 'Mieszko surrendered to Conrad in the fall, and the Treaty of Merseburg required the return of Meissen and Lusatia.'
1033: Conrad II claims the Kingdom of Burgundy against Odo II of Blois.
1033: Lusatia and Meissen come back: the Treaty of Merseburg 'required the return of Meissen and Lusatia', issued at the assembly of July 1033 that 'restored Mieszko to the Polish throne'.
1033: the rest of Lusatia returns to the Empire's shape under the same treaty; Cliopatria adds them in 1034.
1034: Odo's hold on western Burgundy ends no later than the incorporation of the kingdom.
1034: Conrad II incorporates the Kingdom of Burgundy (Arles).
1094: Corsica passes from the Empire's shape to the Republic of Pisa's shape in Cliopatria.
1125: the Salian line ends and the crown passes to Lothair III.
1126: 12 cells in the Lubusz land east of the Oder pass from the Empire's shape to Cliopatria's Kingdom of Poland shape.
1138: the Hohenstaufen succeed Lothair III.
1139: Cliopatria's shape takes Corsica back from the Republic of Pisa's shape.
1147: the Wendish Crusade reaches the Slav coast of Holstein.
1147: Cliopatria's shape drops the Abruzzo cells to the Kingdom of Sicily's shape.
1147: Corsica leaves the Empire's shape for the Republic of Pisa's.
1157: Albert the Bear's Margraviate of Brandenburg takes the Havelland back.
1164: the Pomeranian dukes become vassals within the Empire.
1185: Pomerania passes to Denmark.
1185: the Baltic coast between the Elbe and the Oder leaves the Empire's reach for Denmark.
1188: Cliopatria's shape loses 46 cells of south-eastern France (Loire, Rhône, Ain, Saône-et-Loire) to its Kingdom of France shape (32) and its Arles strip (14).
1198: Bohemia becomes a kingdom within the Empire.
1201: Valdemar of Denmark takes the field against Holstein: 'He defeated and captured the count at the Battle of Stellau in 1201' (Count Adolf III of Holstein).
1203: Holstein and Lübeck fall to Denmark.
1203: the contest over Holstein is settled by the Danish conquest; Danish rule holds until 1223-1227.
1223: the Danes lose their north German holdings.
1227: Bornhöved ends the contest.
1227: the southern Baltic shore comes back to the Empire's side after Bornhöved.
1227: Pomerania is again under the Empire's suzerainty after the Danes leave: 'From the late 12th century, the Duchy of Pomerania was under the suzerainty of the Holy Roman Empire'.
1236: Brandenburg takes the Stargard Land from Pomerania.
1254: the Hohenstaufen line ends.
1259: the Kingdom of Bohemia's vassalage ends in the dossier, not in history: Cliopatria's relation row runs 1202-1259 and its next Bohemian vassalage starts 1314; no page opened ends it.

1259: the Pomeranian vassalage ends in the dossier at the row boundary, not in history; the Duchy of Pomerania page has the Treaty of Landin of 1250 restoring Barnim I's rule over Pomerania, and no end of the Empire's suzerainty.
1259: the Cliopatria row of the directly held Empire ends; the same Empire continues in the row 'Holy Roman Empire Minor States' from 1260.

wars.name: Great Slav Rising
wars.outcome: Slav victory: Havelberg (29 June 983) and Brandenburg (three days later) taken, the Northern and Billung Marches lost, the Elbe line held; annual Imperial campaigns from 985; Henry II allies with the Lutici in 1003.

wars.name: Otto I's conflict with the Byzantine Empire over southern Italy
wars.outcome: Settled in 972: 'the Byzantine Empire accepted Otto's dominion over the principalities of Capua, Benevento and Salerno' and Otto 'retreated from the Byzantine possessions in Apulia and Calabria'.

wars.name: Henry II's wars against Boleslaw I of Poland
wars.outcome: Peace of Bautzen, 30 January 1018 (the fourth treaty after Merseburg 1013): Poland kept Lusatia and Meissen on nominal terms of vassalage; Bohemia stayed with the Empire.

wars.name: Arduin of Ivrea's rebellion
wars.outcome: Henry II crowned King of Italy at Pavia on 14 May 1004; Arduin resigned his margraviate and died on 14 December 1015.

wars.name: Conrad II's war against Poland
wars.outcome: Mieszko II invaded Lusatia in 1028 and surrendered in the fall of 1031; the Treaty of Merseburg required the return of Meissen and Lusatia and was issued at the July 1033 assembly that restored Mieszko.

wars.name: Conrad II's war against Hungary
wars.outcome: Conrad's invasion of 1030 failed in the face of Hungarian scorched earth; in 1031 'Henry gave Hungarian nobles titles to eastern Bavarian lands between the Lajta and Fischa rivers'.

wars.name: Succession to the Kingdom of Burgundy
wars.outcome: Conrad crowned king of Burgundy at Payerne on 2 February 1033, withdrawing to Zürich in March; 'On 1 August 1034, Conrad officially incorporated Burgundy into the Holy Roman Empire' at Geneva.

wars.name: Investiture Controversy
wars.outcome: Ended by the Concordat of Worms in 1122 ('reached an agreement with the Pope and the bishops'); no land changed hands.

wars.name: Wendish Crusade
wars.outcome: Eastern Holstein enters the Empire's shape; the Great Slav Rising page makes the Crusade of 1147 and Albert the Bear's Brandenburg (1157) the start of the resumed eastward settlement.

wars.name: Henry the Lion's campaign against the Pomeranians
wars.outcome: After the Battle of Verchen 'the Pomeranian dukes became vassals of Henry the Lion, of Saxony'; in 1181 the dukes took their duchy as a fief from Barbarossa.

wars.name: Danish conquest of Holstein and Lübeck
wars.outcome: Valdemar II took Count Adolf III of Holstein at Stellau (1201), conquered Lübeck and Holstein (1203), Stade (1214) and Hamburg (1216); captured in 1223, he lost the German lands, was beaten at Mölln (1225) and at Bornhöved (22 July 1227).

wars.name: War with the Lombard League
wars.outcome: Frederick II 'won a great victory over the Lombard League at the Battle of Cortenuova' in November 1237; no border change is drawn.

wars.name: Conflict between Frederick II and the Papacy
wars.outcome: Frederick excommunicated on 29 September 1227 and again in 1239, deposed at Lyon in 1245; he died on 13 December 1250.

certainty.note: Frontiers are the marches, duchies and bishoprics of a feudal empire: the eastern frontier moves with campaigns (983, 1002-1018, 1157, 1227), Italian and Burgundian lands are held with varying autonomy, and no treaty in the period fixes a…
